items.def: Verifies the MLS can be successfully installed, configured, and uninstalled across all supported environments (dependencies, framework compatibility, installation scripts).
Verifies capability to revert to a previously stable state after a degraded or failed deployment; must be performed before deployment to confirm rollback readiness.
Releases an updated model to a small subset of production traffic (e.g., 5% of users), monitoring real-time metrics to detect regressions before full rollout.
Runs a new model in parallel with the current production model in real-time, same requests to both, without affecting live responses; uncovers performance regressions and data drift pre-deployment.
Verifies the model retains acceptable predictive accuracy, consistent behavior, and operational efficiency after conversion from training format to deployment format.
Cross-device: correct performance across deployment targets (mobile, edge, cloud). API testing: standards-compliant interfaces, correct input/output handling, error messages.

items.text: This chapter addresses risks from ML development tools, configuration choices, and deployment mechanisms — not the ML model itself. Approaches include API testing, ML functional performance testing, A/B testing, back-to-back testing, and reviews.
Rollback testing must be performed before deployment to confirm rollback readiness; it may cover only the model or the complete system (e.g., including the data pipeline).
